content.method: source inspection, manager output, runtime Goal audit
findings: worktree.py prepare always calls work_unit.py admit, and admit currently accepts only ready status.
attempt-start transitions the Work Unit to working before the observed workflow called prepare.
the rename Work Unit recorded a permanent BLOCKER-WORKTREE-PREPARE-ORDER before any Git mutation.
repository history records that worktree preparation necessarily precedes execution-init in the documented workflow.
blocker-resolve can return a blocked active attempt to working, but no current manager-owned path can create its missing worktree.
interpretations: future execution needs an explicit prepare-before-attempt contract.
existing valid active attempts need a narrowly validated prepare recovery path without accepting backlog or invalid identities.
limitations: No code mutation or regression test has yet proven the proposed recovery behavior.
